relations.direct_evidence: The printer front seam [0.273,0.565]-[0.512,0.542] and lower output-tray edge [0.318,0.63]-[0.466,0.613] run in the same apparent width direction as the tabletop front boundary [0.167,0.723]-[0.876,0.639]. The printer depth edges [0.297,0.516]-[0.297,0.565] and [0.473,0.498]-[0.507,0.543] are consistent with the same front-facing orientation on the tabletop.
relations.counterevidence: The printer footprint remains inside the visible tabletop boundaries, with front and side edges not crossing the support edges.
relations.visibility_limit: minor rear/base portions of the printer are hidden by the printer body and viewing angle

relations.direct_evidence: The table width edges [0.167,0.723]-[0.876,0.639] and [0.176,0.578]-[0.733,0.515] read as a tabletop rotated in the room; the rear cabinet seam [0.624,0.332]-[1.0,0.358], wall/curtain vertical [0.352,0.0]-[0.354,0.575], and floor seam [0.651,0.802]-[0.848,0.7] provide room references without a visible axis collision.
relations.counterevidence: Visible table legs descend toward the floor in front of the cabinet and do not intersect the rear wall or cabinet surfaces impossibly.
relations.visibility_limit: wall-floor junction is partly hidden by the table, cabinet, curtain, and rug

relations.direct_evidence: The printer occupies roughly one third of the visible tabletop width and less than the table depth, leaving substantial open wooden surface around it; its apparent height and footprint are plausible relative to the table legs, rear cabinet, paper stack, and plant pot.
relations.counterevidence: No nearby furniture or room reference makes the printer appear excessively large or miniature.
relations.visibility_limit: full rear depth of the table is partly occluded by the printer and perspective, but enough surrounding top is visible for scale comparison

relations.direct_evidence: The tabletop and front apron are visibly carried by multiple connected wooden legs: left front leg, left inner/rear visible leg, middle rear visible leg, and right front leg. The front-left and front-right underside load regions have visible vertical members connected below them, and the front apron/rail connects between those supports.
relations.counterevidence: Open negative space is visible under the table, but it is bounded by visible legs rather than showing an exposed unsupported tabletop end.
relations.visibility_limit: rear underside and some foot contacts are partially hidden by the tabletop/apron, cabinet, rug, and lower frame edge

relations.direct_evidence: Both width boundaries and both depth boundaries of the ordinary rectilinear tabletop are visible and connected: near support_front [0.167,0.723]-[0.876,0.639], far support_front [0.176,0.578]-[0.733,0.515], left support_side [0.167,0.723]-[0.176,0.578], and right support_side [0.876,0.639]-[0.733,0.515]. The visible near tabletop width is 0.709 normalized x.
relations.counterevidence: The near and far width edges are continuous wooden boundaries, but the opposite depth-edge mismatch is not explained by any visible hinge, taper, or non-rectangular construction.

relations.direct_evidence: The printer front seam [0.273,0.565]-[0.512,0.542] sits above and in front of the tabletop front boundary [0.167,0.723]-[0.876,0.639]; the rear cabinet seam [0.624,0.332]-[1.0,0.358] remains behind the table, while the floor seam [0.651,0.802]-[0.848,0.7] is below the table legs. These depth orders do not visibly cross or invert.
relations.counterevidence: Table, printer, cabinet, wall, and floor surfaces maintain the expected occlusion order: printer on tabletop, tabletop over legs, legs in front of floor, cabinet behind table.
relations.visibility_limit: support tabletop anatomy has a separate visible side-edge deformation; rear wall-floor contact is partly occluded

relations.direct_evidence: The visible printer base and curved lower side surfaces rest directly on the wooden tabletop with no visible continuous air gap; the body footprint remains inside the tabletop outline rather than hanging beyond an edge.
relations.counterevidence: A small contact shadow and occlusion along the printer underside coincide with the tabletop surface.
relations.visibility_limit: rear underside of the printer is hidden by the body and viewing angle

relations.direct_evidence: Soft contact darkening is visible immediately below the printer base on the tabletop, and the broader sunlight/shadow direction from the left window is consistent across tabletop, floor, and cabinet surfaces.
relations.counterevidence: No reflection, cast shadow, or contact shadow visibly contradicts the printer resting on the table.
relations.visibility_limit: some shadow details are softened by wood grain and diffuse indoor lighting
